content: PPP1R8, also known as the nuclear inhibitor of protein phosphatase 1, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the PPP1R8 gene. This gene produces three distinct isoforms through alternative splicing. Two of these protein isoforms act as specific inhibitors of type 1 serine/threonine protein phosphatases. These isoforms are capable of binding RNA but lack the ability to cleave it. The third isoform, in contrast, does not possess the phosphatase inhibitory function. Instead, it functions as a single-strand endoribonuclease, similar to RNase E found in Escherichia coli. This isoform requires magnesium ions for its enzymatic activity and cleaves RNA at specific sites within A+U-rich regions. Interactions PPP1R8 has been demonstrated to interact with several proteins, including PPP1CA (protein phosphatase 1 catalytic subunit alpha), histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2), SF3B1 (splicing factor 3B subunit 1), EED (embryonic ectoderm development protein), and the EZH2 domain of the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2).
